source.title: Direct lesion evidence for Q17: If consciousness is fundamental, what is the brain doing?
source.author: Codex/Hermes autonomous loop

external_sources.author: M. J. Farah and T. E. Feinberg

external_sources.title: Why is blindsight blind? A new perspective on primary visual cortex, recurrent activity and visual awareness
external_sources.author: Juha Silvanto

external_sources.title: Primary visual cortex, awareness and blindsight

external_sources.author: Brian L. Edlow et al.

source_span.quote: perception and consciousness are dissociated as a result of brain damage

claims.claim_text: Brain damage can dissociate perceptual processing from conscious perception across several visual syndromes, so a brain-role theory must explain content-specific losses without immediately equating all processing with awareness.
claims.hetu: lesion syndromes show separable conscious and nonconscious perceptual capacities
claims.sadhya: brain-role theories need content-specific transformation rules
claims.vyapti_statement: Where focal damage dissociates processing from awareness, a viable theory must explain which content is lost, spared, or covertly processed.

falsifier.condition: A systematic lesion review finds no stable dissociation between perceptual processing and conscious perception after controlling for task/report confounds.

claims.reasoning: This supports a mechanistic interface account at the content level, while also blocking the overclaim that every neural process is conscious or that lesion evidence settles metaphysics.

source_span.quote: local read-out from specific brain regions

claims.claim_text: Blindsight after V1 damage can preserve local visual discriminations while phenomenal visual awareness is absent or reduced, pressuring theories to separate local information processing from globally available experience.
claims.hetu: V1-lesion cases can show visual discrimination without ordinary visual awareness
claims.sadhya: brain-role theories must distinguish information availability from manifest content
claims.vyapti_statement: Where damage removes awareness while preserving limited discrimination, the explanatory target is the transformation of access/availability, not a simple all-or-nothing production claim.

falsifier.condition: Robust evidence shows blindsight performance is fully explained by residual conscious vision or response bias rather than dissociated processing.

claims.reasoning: The claim supports interface-style access models and can be accommodated by filter views if filtering is made operational. It does not prove that V1 generates consciousness.

source_span.quote: insufficient evidence in support of the former proposition

claims.claim_text: Review evidence leaves open whether V1 directly contributes to awareness or primarily supplies visual input to wider perceptual systems, so focal-lesion data constrains mechanisms without settling the substrate of awareness.
claims.hetu: V1 lesion evidence admits conduit and direct-generator interpretations
claims.sadhya: lesion evidence should be represented as mechanism pressure with a metaphysical boundary
claims.vyapti_statement: If the same lesion pattern is compatible with multiple mechanistic interpretations, the engine must keep the crux open rather than treating the lesion as decisive.

falsifier.condition: Convergent lesion, stimulation, and recovery evidence shows V1 is uniquely necessary as the direct generator of visual awareness rather than a major input pathway.

claims.reasoning: This is a boundary claim. It protects the benchmark from turning lesion specificity into a settled production thesis.

source_span.quote: lesions confined to the upper pons can cause coma

claims.claim_text: Brainstem lesion mapping indicates that damage to upper pontine tegmental regions can cause coma, so any brain-role theory must account for neural dependence of arousal and consciousness level, not only contents.
claims.hetu: specific brainstem lesions are associated with loss of consciousness level
claims.sadhya: brain-role theories must explain arousal-level dependence as well as content transformation
claims.vyapti_statement: Where localized injury reliably disrupts consciousness level, a viable nonproduction account must supply an operational dependence relation rather than a loose receiver analogy.

falsifier.condition: Large lesion-network studies fail to associate brainstem/arousal-network damage with impaired consciousness level after controlling for systemic injury severity.

claims.reasoning: This is the strongest lesion pressure in the packet because it concerns consciousness level. It still constrains rather than decides metaphysical production, since dependence and generation remain distinct hypotheses.

source_span.quote: preserved brain networks in patients who seem unresponsive

claims.claim_text: Disorders-of-consciousness recovery work shows that preserved or reactivated brain networks can support covert consciousness and recovery prediction, keeping lesion evidence network-sensitive rather than a simple destroyed/not-destroyed verdict.
claims.hetu: covert consciousness and recovery can depend on preserved or reactivated networks
claims.sadhya: lesion evidence should be modeled as network-level constraint rather than single-region proof
claims.vyapti_statement: Where preserved network structure predicts covert consciousness or recovery, the brain-role question concerns dynamic organization and intervention response, not merely local damage.

falsifier.condition: Covert consciousness and recovery predictions show no robust relation to preserved or reactivated neural networks in high-quality prospective cohorts.

claims.reasoning: This supports mechanism-shaped explanations while warning against simple lesion localism. It pressures appearance-only views to explain predictive utility, but does not refute them.
